notes: Every price below is copied verbatim from the current /shop page. No price was invented or adjusted.
shortDescription is the current site's own copy, lightly cleaned (trailing punctuation normalised, exclamation marks removed, sentence case kept).
longDescription is NEW copy. It only restates facts that appear on the current site (product description, /about, /shokupan). No hydration %, bake time, weight, shelf life or ingredient is invented.

allergens.contains = stated or unavoidable (wheat flour in a bread; pistachio in a pistachio bun). allergens.likely = inferred from the product type and NOT confirmed by the founders. Do not print 'likely' allergens as fact on the site; print them as 'may contain'.
existingImage is a filename in research/site-snapshot/images/. null means no usable shot exists and the product needs to be photographed.
badges.bestseller is applied ONLY to the 8 products the current home page lists under 'Featured Specialties / Our customer favourites this week'. Nothing else claims popularity.

categories.label: Breads
categories.description: Japanese milk loaves, baked eggless. Square-cut, fine crumb, made to be sliced. This is the range Fillo Bakes is built on.

categories.label: An Pan
categories.description: Soft milk buns with a filling in the middle. Ours are filled with cream rather than the red bean paste of the Tokyo original.

categories.label: Kare Pan
categories.description: The savoury stuffed bun. Crisp outside, soft inside, spiced filling. Two on the menu right now.

categories.label: Pies and Strudels
categories.description: Layered pastry, folded and baked. Seven of them, sweet and savoury, from ₹99. The easiest place to start.

categories.label: Fruit Sandos
categories.description: Our shokupan, crusts off, whipped cream and fruit in the middle. Cut so the fruit shows. Made the day you get it.

categories.label: Weekly Specials
categories.description: One or two bakes that run for a week and then stop. Check the van route the week they are on.
categories.emptyState: Nothing special this week. The next one goes up on a Monday.

products.name: Milk Shokupan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bread.
products.longDescription: This is the loaf the bakery started with, and the one that took the longest to get right without eggs. Fine, pillowy crumb, a light sweetness, and a square slice that holds its shape under a toaster or a sando filling. Everything in the Fruit Sandos range is built on it.
products.notes: Called out as the signature bread on /about and given its own SEO page at /shokupan. Treat as the hero SKU.

products.name: Japanese Marble Bread
products.shortDescription: A soft, fluffy milk bread (shokupan) with swirls of chocolate.
products.longDescription: The milk shokupan with a chocolate dough folded through it, so every slice comes out with its own pattern. Sweet enough to eat plain, plain enough to toast. Good with coffee and nothing else.

products.name: Blue Pea Bread
products.shortDescription: A naturally blue, ultra-soft milk bread (shokupan) infused with butterfly pea flower. No artificial colour, just clean botanical colour.
products.longDescription: The colour comes from butterfly pea flower, not from a bottle. It is the same soft shokupan crumb underneath, so it behaves like any other loaf on a toaster or under jam. Children tend to ask for this one twice.
products.notes: The 'no artificial colour' claim is on the current site and is a real differentiator. Keep it, and keep it exact.

products.name: Chocolate Shokupan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese chocolate bread.
products.longDescription: Chocolate worked through the whole dough rather than swirled, so the loaf is dark right the way through. Same soft crumb, less sweetness than a cake, and it toasts well. If you want the pattern instead, take the Marble.

products.name: Strawberry An Pan
products.shortDescription: Japanese milk bun filled with fresh strawberry and cream.
products.longDescription: A soft milk bun split and filled with strawberry and cream. It is a bun, not a pastry, so the outside stays tender rather than crisp. Eat it the day it reaches you.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list.

products.name: Custard An Pan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bun filled with a delicate custard cream. Fluffy and smooth.
products.longDescription: The plainest of the buns and the one people come back for. Milk bun, custard cream, nothing else competing. Eggless custard is harder to get smooth than most people assume.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list.

products.name: Choco An Pan
products.shortDescription: Japanese chocolate bun filled with a rich, velvety chocolate. Double delight.
products.longDescription: Chocolate bun with chocolate inside, which is exactly as direct as it sounds. Softer and less sweet than a pastry, and it travels well in a lunch box. The one to order for children.
products.notes: Current URL is /product/choco-la, which matches nothing a customer would search. 301 choco-la -> choco-an-pan.

products.name: Pistachio An Pan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bun filled with a rich pistachio cream.
products.longDescription: Pistachio cream in a milk bun, and the flavour carries without being sugary. Contains pistachio, so it is the one bun on the menu to skip if there is a nut allergy at the table. Ordered most often alongside the Tiramisu.
products.notes: Only SKU with a confirmed tree-nut allergen. Surface a nut flag on the card, not just the detail page.

products.name: Tiramisu An Pan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bun filled with a tiramisu cream blend.
products.longDescription: Coffee and cream in bun form, for people who find a whole dessert too much. Mild rather than bitter. Best with a second coffee, which rather defeats the point.
products.notes: NO PRODUCT PHOTO EXISTS. Needs a shoot before launch. Contains coffee; confirm with founders whether caffeine should be declared.

products.name: Cookie n Cream An Pan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bun filled with cookie and cream, topped with Oreo.
products.longDescription: Cookies-and-cream filling in a milk bun, finished with crushed Oreo on top. It is the sweetest thing on the menu and it does not pretend otherwise. Share one rather than ordering two.
products.notes: Uses a third-party branded biscuit (Oreo). Check trademark usage before printing the brand name in headings.

products.name: Banana Biscoff An Pan
products.shortDescription: Soft Japanese milk bun filled with a banana and Biscoff cream, topped with fresh banana.
products.longDescription: Banana and Biscoff cream inside, fresh banana on top. The fresh fruit means it is a same-day bun, not something to keep for tomorrow. Order it for a morning, not for a Sunday stock-up.
products.notes: /product/banana-biscoff currently returns Product Not Found. 301 to this slug.

products.name: Seoul Spice
products.shortDescription: Fiery gochujang-glazed sweet potato with a bold Korean kick.
products.longDescription: Sweet potato glazed in gochujang, wrapped in a karepan shell. The sweetness of the potato takes the edge off the chilli, but this is still the hotter of the two kare pan. If you like heat, start here.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list. Gochujang usually contains soy and wheat; confirm with founders.

products.name: Tex Mex Zest
products.shortDescription: Zesty jalapeno and bell peppers with three cheeses.
products.longDescription: Jalapeno, bell pepper and three cheeses in a soft bun. Warm rather than punishing on the heat, and it reheats better than most things here. The one that disappears fastest at a table of four.
products.notes: NO PRODUCT PHOTO EXISTS despite being a featured product and one of only four working product pages. Highest-priority shoot.

products.name: Bangalore Bloom
products.shortDescription: Mixed vegetables and potato with subtle spices in a soft, airy puff.
products.longDescription: Vegetable and potato in a light puff, spiced gently enough for a child and priced at ₹99. It is the cheapest thing on the menu and the one most people try first. Closer to a bakery puff you already know than anything else here.
products.notes: Lowest price point on the menu (₹99). Use it as the trial SKU in acquisition copy.

products.name: Kyoto Curry
products.shortDescription: A delicate Japanese-style vegetable curry wrapped in golden pastry.
products.longDescription: Japanese curry is milder and sweeter than the Indian kind, and this pastry keeps it that way. Vegetables in a smooth curry sauce, folded into pastry and baked. A good first taste of the Japanese side of the menu.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list. Currently one of only four working product pages.

products.name: Calcutta Blaze
products.shortDescription: Spicy paneer tossed in silky tonkatsu sauce.
products.longDescription: Paneer in tonkatsu sauce, which is the sweet-sharp Japanese brown sauce, with the heat turned up. An unlikely pairing that works because the sauce is already sweet. The most Indian-tasting thing in the pastry range.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list. Tonkatsu sauce is typically soy-based; confirm.

products.name: Umami Melt
products.shortDescription: Creamy mushroom and cheese with a rich, savoury depth.
products.longDescription: Mushroom and cheese, cooked down until the filling is thick rather than wet. No chilli at all, which makes it the savoury pastry for people who do not want heat. Best eaten warm.
products.notes: On the current home page's Featured Specialties list.

products.name: Korean Whisper
products.shortDescription: Spring onion, creamy cheese and garlic in a flaky Korean-inspired shell.
products.longDescription: Spring onion, garlic and cream cheese in flaky pastry, taking its cue from Korean garlic bread. Rich, garlicky, and not remotely subtle. Order it if you like garlic bread and want it to be a pastry.

products.name: Orchard Melt
products.shortDescription: Warm spiced apple compote in folded crisp layers.
products.longDescription: Spiced apple in layered pastry, which is the strudel most people already have in mind. Crisp on the outside, soft in the middle, and warm from the oven if the van reaches you early. A customer on the current site calls it comfort food, which is fair.
products.notes: Named in a testimonial on the current home page: 'The dessert strudels are unreal. Orchard Melt is comfort food at its finest.' Use as a review pull-quote.

products.name: Mawa Melt
products.shortDescription: Milky mawa with gentle cardamom notes and a crumble.
products.longDescription: Mawa and cardamom in a pastry, which puts a mithai shop inside a strudel. Sweet in the Indian way rather than the European one. The bridge item on the menu, and the easiest one to explain to a grandparent.
products.notes: Current copy ends with 'Ooh lala', which does not survive the new voice. Removed.

products.name: Fruit Sando
products.shortDescription: A fruit sandwich on our Milk Shokupan, layered with whipped cream and seasonal fruit.
products.longDescription: Crustless shokupan, whipped cream and seasonal fruit, cut so the fruit shows in the face of the slice. The fruit changes with what is good that week, so no two months look the same. Made the morning it goes out.
products.notes: NO PHOTO. All three sandos currently share one identical description on the live site, which is a real content bug. This rewrite differentiates them. Confirm with founders which fruits actually go in the base Fruit Sando.

products.name: Strawberry Cream Fruit Sando
products.shortDescription: A fruit sando on our Milk Shokupan, with strawberry cream and seasonal fruit.
products.longDescription: The same crustless shokupan sando, with the whipped cream turned pink with strawberry. Fruit is layered so the cut face shows a pattern. This and the custard version are the two to send as a gift.
products.notes: Image match is INFERRED from the photo (pink cream, kiwi, orange, grape) rather than from a filename. Confirm before publishing. /product/strawberry-cream currently 404s; 301 it here.

products.name: Custard Cream Fruit Sando
products.shortDescription: A fruit sando on our Milk Shokupan, with custard cream and seasonal fruit.
products.longDescription: Custard cream instead of plain whipped, which makes it the richer of the two. Seasonal fruit set through the middle and the crusts taken off. Same-day only, like the rest of the sandos.
products.notes: Image match is INFERRED from the photo (yellow custard cream, orange, grape). Confirm before publishing.
